# Problem 1

```{r load-noaa}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

data("ny_noaa", package = "p8105.datasets")

missing_table =
  ny_noaa |>
  summarize(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_fraction"
  )

missing_table |>
  mutate(
    missing_percentage =
      scales::percent(missing_fraction, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  select(variable, missing_percentage) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Variable", "Missing observations")
  )
```

The dataset contains `r format(nrow(ny_noaa), big.mark = ",")`
observations and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables from
`r n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)` weather stations in New York State.
Each row represents a station-date observation between 1981 and 2010.
Variables include station ID, date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth,
and daily maximum and minimum temperatures.

Missingness is most substantial for maximum and minimum temperature,
with 43.7% of observations missing for each variable. Snow depth has
22.8% missingness, followed by snowfall at 14.7% and precipitation at
5.6%. Station IDs and dates have no missing values. This limits
comparisons because summaries may be based on different subsets of
station-days.


```{r clean-noaa}
noaa =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )

snow_counts =
  noaa |>
  filter(!is.na(snow)) |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE)

snow_counts |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Snowfall (mm)", "Number of observations"),
    caption = "Ten most commonly observed snowfall values"
  )
```

Separate year, month, and day variables were created.
Maximum and minimum temperatures were converted to degrees Celsius,
and precipitation was converted to millimeters. Snowfall and snow
depth were already measured in millimeters.

The most common snowfall value is `r snow_counts$snow[1]` mm,
with `r format(snow_counts$n[1], big.mark = ",")` observations.
Zero snowfall is expected to be common because many station-days
have no snowfall. Common positive values may reflect rounding and
conversion from measurements originally recorded in inches.


```{r monthly-temperature, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
station_temperature =
  noaa |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    observed_days = sum(!is.na(tmax)),
    mean_tmax = if (all(is.na(tmax))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

station_temperature |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average maximum temperature by station and year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean maximum temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

Each line represents a weather station. The panels allow comparison
of seasonal differences and year-to-year variation. Differences
among stations may reflect geography, while changes shared by
many stations may reflect regional weather patterns.

```{r temperature-extremes}
station_temperature |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_tmax)) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  slice_min(mean_tmax, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(month, id, year, mean_tmax, observed_days) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = "Lowest station-year mean temperature in each month"
  )
```

The lowest January station-year mean maximum temperature was −13.4°C
at station USC00301723 in 1982. The lowest July value was 14.0°C at
station USC00308962 in 1988. Both averages use 31 observed days, so
neither is explained by having only a few daily observations. These
values warrant further inspection, but station location and measurement
quality should be checked before treating them as errors.


```{r temperature-snowfall, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
temperature_plot =
  noaa |>
  filter(!is.na(tmin), !is.na(tmax)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin_2d(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10") +
  labs(
    title = "Minimum versus maximum temperature",
    x = "Minimum temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

snowfall_plot =
  noaa |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = as.character(seq(1981, 2010, by = 5))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Positive snowfall below 100 mm",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

temperature_plot + snowfall_plot
```

The two-dimensional binned plot summarizes the relationship between
daily minimum and maximum temperatures. Color indicates the number
of observations within each bin, reducing the overplotting that would
occur in a scatterplot of the full dataset.

The snowfall boxplots compare the median, spread, and upper tails
of positive snowfall below 100 mm across years. Because zero snowfall
and events of 100 mm or more are excluded, this figure does not
describe annual snowfall totals or snowfall frequency.


# Problem 2

```{r import-nhanes}
# Find the header below any introductory metadata.
covar_lines = read_lines("data/nhanes_covar.csv")

header_row = which(
  str_detect(covar_lines, regex("SEQN", ignore_case = TRUE))
)[1]

covar_raw =
  read_csv(
    "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
    skip = header_row - 1,
    na = c("", "NA", ".")
  ) |>
  rename_with(tolower)

covar =
  covar_raw |>
  drop_na() |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  mutate(
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Less than high school",
        "High school equivalent",
        "More than high school"
      )
    )
  )

accel =
  read_csv("data/nhanes_accel.csv") |>
  rename_with(tolower)

nhanes =
  covar |>
  inner_join(accel, by = "seqn") |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^min\\d+$"),
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    minute = as.integer(minute),
    hour = (minute - 1) / 60
  )

participants =
  nhanes |>
  distinct(seqn, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(all_of(names(covar)))
```

Participants younger than 21 and those with missing demographic
information were excluded. Sex and education were encoded as factors,
with education ordered from less than high school to more than high
school. Activity measurements were reshaped into one row per
participant per minute, retaining the original demographic variables.

The merged dataset contains `r n_distinct(nhanes$seqn)` participants
and `r format(nrow(nhanes), big.mark = ",")` participant-minute
observations. MIMS measures activity intensity, and the hour variable
expresses time since midnight.


```{r nhanes-demographics, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
demographic_counts =
  participants |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )

demographic_counts |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Education", "Male", "Female"),
    caption = "Participant counts by education and sex"
  )

participants |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Age distributions by sex and education",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Age (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )

participants |>
  group_by(education, sex) |>
  summarize(
    participants = n(),
    median_age = median(age),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = "Participant counts and median ages"
  )
```

The more-than-high-school group is the largest, with 115 participants
(56 men and 59 women). The less-than-high-school group includes
27 men and 28 women, while the high-school-equivalent group includes
35 men and 23 women.

Participants with more than a high school education are younger:
median ages are 43.5 years for men and 41 years for women, compared
with 60 and 61 years in the less-than-high-school group. Within the
high-school-equivalent group, women have a higher median age than
men (62 versus 53 years). These age differences should be considered
when comparing activity across groups.


```{r nhanes-total-activity, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
daily_activity =
  nhanes |>
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) |>
  summarize(
    observed_minutes = sum(!is.na(mims)),
    total_activity = if (all(is.na(mims))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      sum(mims, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

daily_activity |>
  summarize(
    minimum_observed_minutes = min(observed_minutes),
    maximum_observed_minutes = max(observed_minutes)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Activity measurement coverage per participant"
  )

daily_activity |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Total daily activity by age, sex, and education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total daily activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10))

daily_activity |>
  group_by(education, sex) |>
  summarize(
    median_total_activity = median(total_activity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = "Median total daily activity by group"
  )
```
All 228 participants have 1,440 observed minutes, so daily activity
totals are based on complete 24-hour coverage.

In the less-than-high-school group, men have a higher median total
activity than women (14,935.1 versus 13,336.2 MIMS). Women have higher
medians in the high-school-equivalent group (12,062.8 versus 11,220.8)
and the more-than-high-school group (13,977.4 versus 11,977.5).
Thus, the direction of the sex difference varies across education
groups. These unadjusted summaries do not account for differences
in age composition and do not establish causal effects.


```{r nhanes-time-course, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
minute_activity =
  nhanes |>
  group_by(education, sex, minute, hour) |>
  summarize(
    mean_mims = if (all(is.na(mims))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(mims, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

minute_activity |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = mean_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    span = 0.15,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6),
    limits = c(0, 24)
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Average activity throughout the day",
    x = "Hour since midnight",
    y = "Mean activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10))
```

The three panels compare activity timing and intensity across education
categories, with color identifying sex. Faint lines show minute-specific
group means, while smooth curves emphasize broader daily patterns.
These curves describe group averages rather than individual
participants' activity trajectories.

# Problem 3

```{r p3-import}
library(tidyverse)

dir.create("data/citibike", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

if (!file.exists("data/citibike.zip")) {
  local_zip = path.expand("~/Downloads/citibike.zip")

  if (file.exists(local_zip)) {
    file.copy(local_zip, "data/citibike.zip")
  } else {
    download.file(
      "https://p8105.com/data/citibike.zip",
      "data/citibike.zip",
      mode = "wb"
    )
  }
}

unzip(
  "data/citibike.zip",
  exdir = "data/citibike",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# Extract the four inner zip files.
inner_zips = list.files(
  "data/citibike",
  pattern = "\\.zip$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

inner_zips = inner_zips[
  !str_detect(inner_zips, "__MACOSX|/\\._")
]

for (zip_path in inner_zips) {
  unzip(
    zip_path,
    exdir = "data/citibike",
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
}

csv_files = list.files(
  "data/citibike",
  pattern = "\\.csv$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

csv_files = csv_files[
  !str_detect(csv_files, "__MACOSX|/\\._")
]

csv_files = csv_files[
  !duplicated(tolower(basename(csv_files)))
]

csv_files = csv_files[
  basename(csv_files) %in% c(
    "Jan 2020 Citi.csv",
    "Jan 2024 Citi.csv",
    "July 2020 Citi.csv",
    "July 2024 Citi.csv"
  )
]
if (length(csv_files) != 4) {
  stop(
    "Expected 4 distinct CSV files; found ",
    length(csv_files),
    ": ",
    paste(basename(csv_files), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

bike = map_dfr(csv_files, function(path) {
  file_name = str_to_lower(basename(path))

  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(
      year = as.integer(str_extract(file_name, "20\\d{2}")),
      month = if_else(
        str_detect(file_name, "jan"),
        "January",
        "July"
      )
    )
}) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = c("January", "July")),
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c(
        "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
        "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"
      )
    ),
    member_casual = factor(
      member_casual,
      levels = c("casual", "member"),
      labels = c("Casual", "Member")
    ),
    rideable_type = factor(
      rideable_type,
      levels = c("classic_bike", "electric_bike"),
      labels = c("Classic", "Electric")
    )
  )
```

The combined dataset contains `r format(nrow(bike), big.mark = ",")`
rides and `r ncol(bike)` variables. Each row is one ride.
Variables include duration in minutes, bike type, membership,
weekday, and starting and ending stations. Year and month were
added from file names. The data contain a 1% sample of rides
under four hours in January and July of 2020 and 2024.

## Ride counts

```{r p3-counts}
bike |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  arrange(year, month) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Year", "Month", "Casual", "Member"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )
```

Members account for most rides in all four periods. July has more
rides than January in both years, and both months have more rides
in 2024 than in 2020. July 2024 has the largest count, with 47,156 rides.


```{r p3-stations}
bike |>
  filter(
    year == 2024,
    month == "July",
    !is.na(start_station_name),
    start_station_name != ""
  ) |>
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Starting station", "Rides"),
    caption = "Top five starting stations in July 2024"
  )
```



```{r p3-weekdays, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
median_duration =
  bike |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(
    median_minutes = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

median_duration |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = weekdays,
      y = median_minutes,
      color = factor(year),
      group = factor(year)
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ month) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Median duration (minutes)",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

Median rides are longer in July than January and shorter in 2024
than 2020 on every weekday. Weekend medians are higher than weekday
medians in both July samples and January 2020. January 2024 shows
less variation, without a consistent weekend increase.

```{r p3-duration, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
bike |>
  filter(year == 2024) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = member_casual,
      y = duration,
      fill = rideable_type
    )
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.alpha = 0.15,
    outlier.size = 0.4,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ month) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Ride duration (minutes)",
    fill = "Bike type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

Median durations are higher in July than January for every
membership and bike-type group. Casual riders have longer median
rides than members for both bike types. Among casual riders,
classic-bike rides have higher medians than electric-bike rides;
among members, electric-bike rides have slightly higher medians.
